notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0098.tlg001.1st1K-gr: The lemma has Γελλώ in the nominative; it is rendered as the comparative proverb 'fonder of children than Gello', which would normally take the genitive.

nodes.text: 'More fond of children than Gello': [said] of those who died before their time, or of those who love their children but ruin them by indulgence. For Gello was a maiden, and since she died before her time, the Lesbians say that her ghost haunts little children, and they attribute the deaths of those who die untimely to her. Sappho mentions her.
